title: The Streets Decide
text: The crowd that put you in the palace took it back. You left through the kitchen.

title: Beloved Unto Death
text: They loved you so much they stopped needing the rest of the government. Then they stopped needing you.

title: Insufficient Funds
text: The treasury bounced its own cheque. The creditors sent a new leader with the bailout.

title: Owned
text: The people who paid for everything would now like a receipt. It has your office on it.

title: Nobody in Charge
text: The last policeman went home. So did everyone else. The palace is a squat now.

title: Security Concern
text: The security services concluded that you were the last remaining threat to security.

title: Out of Office
text: There was no ministry left to sign your removal, so nobody did. You simply stopped being in charge.

title: Pending Review
text: Your removal was approved by all forty-one committees. It took nine years. You were long gone.

title: Conceded
text: You lost. You said so on television, which is more than most manage. The moving van came Tuesday.

title: Change of Management
text: The generals thanked you for your service in a short broadcast. You were not invited to it.

title: Under Its Own Weight
text: The lights went out for the last time, and nobody in the building knew which switch it was.

title: Still Standing
text: The country neither fell nor flew. Historians argue about whether that counts.

title: Orbit
text: The first ship left on time. The people who built it remembered who let them.

title: The Long Way Down
text: Five centuries on, the capital is a ruin with a gift shop. The guide says the fall took everyone. The tourists still ask who started it.

title: The Oldest Argument
text: Five centuries on, the parliament still sits, the deficit is still open and the trains are still late. Nobody alive has seen it end, or wants to.

title: The Far Shore
text: Five centuries on, ships leave for other stars as routinely as trains once left for the coast. Nobody remembers who first let them go.

title: A Quiet Arrangement
text: You were not removed. You were kept, like a signature on a file, by people who had the file.

title: Removed by Vote
text: The chamber found against you by nine votes. It was the last institution still able to count.

title: An Internal Matter
text: The man you made powerful decided the arrangement had become inefficient. The state funeral was very well attended.

title: A Standing Invitation
text: A friendly country offered you a house by a lake. You took it while the offer was still phrased as an offer.

title: Leader for Life
text: They gave you the title, the portrait and the rest of your life in the same building. It was a long life.

title: Handed Over
text: You left on a Tuesday, on time, to someone competent. The country barely noticed, which was the achievement.

title: Insufficiently Committed
text: The list you started reached your own name. You signed it yourself, which they said showed real discipline.

title: Nobody Came
text: The people who knocked on doors for you stopped knocking. There was no announcement. There was just nobody there.

title: Funding Withdrawn
text: The people who paid for all of it stopped paying for all of it. The campaign office lights went out first.

title: They Won
text: The count came in on time, was not disputed, and was not close. {rival} gave a gracious speech about continuity.

title: The Last Signature
text: The enemy would sign with anyone but you, so you signed and resigned the same afternoon. The pen is in a museum now. So is the war.

title: Contempt of Court
text: The court held you in contempt. The army was asked to choose between you and the court, and chose the court, politely.

title: In Receivership
text: The lenders run the budget now. They kept your office open for the photographs, and then the photographs stopped.

title: Taking Responsibility
text: You read the name in the chamber and resigned before anyone could call a vote. It is the only resignation speech the country still quotes.

title: The General Strike
text: Everything stopped at once: the trains, the ports, the presses that would have printed your side of it. When it all started again, it started without you.

title: Condemned
text: The block came down on a Sunday, empty by luck and nothing else. The report that condemned it was found in the rubble, unopened. The inquiry named you on page one.

title: The Long Blackout
text: The lights went out in January and stayed out for eleven days. The country read about the end of your government by candlelight.

title: The Last Shift
text: You went to the gate on the last shift and told them nothing you had done would have saved it. They let you finish. You resigned in the morning.

title: The Grey March
text: The pensioners marched on the capital at walking pace. It took them a week. It took you an afternoon to go.

title: In Those Words
text: You said it on camera, in those words: that it had been a mistake, and that you had known. No government had said both before. It was your last day in office.

title: Under New Management
text: The cartel never took the palace. It never needed to: it had the licences, the police and the paperwork, and in the end it had you.

title: The Breakout
text: Four thousand prisoners walked out of a prison nobody was paid to guard. Most of them were back by Christmas. You were not.

title: The Emergency
text: The emergency powers were renewed every month, until the general who held them renewed them without asking you. The cameras recorded it.

title: The Correction
text: Your last act in office was a correction, printed on the front page in the same size as the lie. Nobody had seen one before. People kept it.

title: The Crowded Bench
text: By the end the highest court had more seats than the parliament, and sat more often. It ruled your government unlawful, a hundred and four to three.

title: The Run
text: Everyone wanted their money on the same morning. By noon the banks had shut their doors, and by evening so had your government.

title: Continuity
text: The term limit went, as your deputy proposed. So did you, a year later, when he proposed that as well. The country got its continuity.

title: The Quiet
text: With no paper left to tell you, nobody did. You learned your government had fallen from the one channel still allowed to say so, which was yours.

title: Victory Declared
text: You declared victory over the fever and held a parade to prove it. The fever came to the parade too, and the inquiry you had not held was held about you.

title: The Posters
text: You spent the desalination money on posters saying whose rationing it had been. The next drought came before the plant would have, and so did the crowds.

title: The Model's Advice
text: You postponed the election, as advised. The model then advised that the office itself was inefficient, and every ministry agreed, having been told to.

title: The Family Firm
text: You named your eldest successor. The family met to agree the timing, without you, and it turned out to be sooner than you had in mind.

title: The Blessing
text: You asked for the blessing and got it, with conditions, then with a list, then with a successor the cardinal had chosen some time before.

title: The Closed Counties
text: The families closed the registry, then the roads, then the counties. You governed what was left, from a capital that had become one of their estates.

title: The Country Decided
text: You lost the referendum by nine thousand votes and conceded before midnight. You resigned in the morning, having asked the country, and been told.

title: Clean Hands
text: You prosecuted all nine, including the man who got you elected, and then resigned, since he had. The commission's last volume is about you. It is short.

title: The Town Council
text: You made the charter policy and stood for the council of the town you grew up in. You won it by four votes, and never looked back.

title: The Job You Wanted
text: You put the engineers' names on the plaque and your own on an application to the programme. They took you, in the end, as its oldest trainee.

title: Given Back
text: You gave the party back to the people who wrote its manifesto, and the leadership with it. They kept most of your promises, and reminded you of the rest.
